detail.longDescription: I hired a marketing co-founder and she found me a job Not the plan. We're three people building a startup. She runs go-to-market. A couple of weeks in she's out doing her actual job, talking to people, and a message lands on my phone: do you know any dev who can ship fast with claude but still owns the architecture I read it like...ummm..what? First because it's a strange way to get a job. You bring someone on to sell your thing, they go out and sell your thing, and what comes back is a role with your name on it. I did not have "hire a marketing person, receive job leads" written down anywhere. Second because of how the ask was phrased. Nobody said Python. Nobody said years of experience. Nobody named a framework, a cloud, or a stack. The entire requirement was two clauses, and the second one is carrying all the weight. Ships fast with Claude. Fine. That is close to table stakes now. If you are not moving faster than you were last year, someone on the other side of the table is. But still owns the architecture. That is the job. It assumes the default is that you do not. That is a hiring manager pricing in something they have already watched happen: output went up, and somewhere in there the person shipping it stopped being able to explain it. You can see the shape of the problem from the shape of the ask. They are not looking for someone who writes less code. They are looking for someone who can still answer for it. Why this service and not that one. What happens when this call times out. Which of these three things is load-bearing and which two you could delete tomorrow. An agent will write all of it. An agent will not be in the room when it breaks, and it will not be the name on the approval when someone asks how this got in. I think this is what job descriptions quietly turn into over the next couple of years. Not "can you build it." Everyone can build it. Do you understand what you built. Anyway. I did know someone. Me. Which is its own kind of weird, because I am supposed to be the one hiring. Opportunities do not really arrive where you point yourself. They arrive through the surface area other people create on your behalf. Get a co-founder who talks to strangers. # programming # productivity # ai # beginners # software # coding # development # engineering # inclusive # community Hired a marketing co-founder and she found me a job
